cultural.vision_reason: A long cotton handkerchief ('batistă') with polychrome twill-woven bands and lace trim, a type of textile associated with Romanian and Csángó folk dress traditions; the woven pattern and lace edging are consistent with a handmade regional textile.

physical.title: handkerchief (?)
physical.summary: A long cotton handkerchief (?), a 'batistă', with polychrome bands.  Rectangular, with twill woven bands, worked in wool and synthetic yarns, a mirror image about the centre line: maroon, green, yellow, blue, orange, purple and red patterned bands separated by two fine red bands on the natural cream cotton 'ground'.  The patterning at each end is denser, making the cloth thicker, with little cream 'ground' in between; oval shaped patterning.  Additional yarns used: pink, lime green and lilac and thin gold-coloured plastic (?) tinsel thread.  Cream cotton lacework trim (commercially made) is stitched to all four sides.
